confidence_note: Gratitude finding and foreboding joy from interview and summaries; sources disagree on which book first uses the term.
facts: Guidepost 4: Cultivating Gratitude and Joy: Letting Go of Scarcity and Fear of the Dark.
Brown never met anyone able to feel joy without regularly practicing gratitude.
Foreboding joy: when joy arrives, fear of loss and imagined catastrophe, for example a parent looking at a child.
Joyful people respond by practicing gratitude.
Painful emotions cannot be numbed selectively; numbing the dark numbs joy too.
scene_details: a parent over a sleeping child
opening_idea: A jolt of fear over a sleeping child.

lessons.idea: When joy arrives, name what you have.

reflect_final: This week, what fear of loss crossed your mind in a good moment?

use_cases.move: Right now they're here and healthy; I'm grateful, out loud.

use_cases.situation: Worst case during a good day
use_cases.move: This is foreboding joy; I name three things.

use_cases.situation: Friend says what if it falls through
use_cases.move: Enjoy first; name three things you're grateful for.

pocket_idea: When joy arrives, don't rehearse the loss: name three things you have now.

conversation_variants.punchline_idea: Everyone able to feel joy practiced gratitude.
